name: Germany
oneLiner: Meyer classes Germany as consensual and direct in feedback, and institutions such as ASPICE and codetermination support quality.
intro: For Germany, the sources are the Culture Map, Hofstede, official statistics and law. The picture is national, and the spread within the country is wide. Regulated industries such as automotive and Berlin startups, for example, have quite different cultures. Germany has plenty of national surveys on error culture and labor-court rulings that reach into engineering work, but no study was found that looks directly at code review culture.

design.text: Meyer's Culture Map (2014) places Germany near the principles-first end of Persuading and the linear-time end of Scheduling. In her description, Germans prefer to reason from principles to conclusions and to keep to the plan.

sources.title: Erin Meyer — Eight-scale Tool for Mapping Cultural Differences (chart: The Culture Map, 2014)

design.text: Automotive SPICE, maintained by VDA QMC, is a de facto condition of doing business in the car industry. According to itemis, OEMs require suppliers to reach Level 2 to 3, with bidirectional traceability between requirements, design and tests. This is a customer requirement, not a law.

sources.title: itemis — What is Automotive SPICE?
VDA QMC — Automotive SPICE PAM v4.0

failure.text: A Randstad-ifo HR survey (Q3 2026, 469 companies) found mistakes discussed openly at 28% of firms with 500+ staff and 62% of firms with 49 or fewer. 34% of large firms said their error culture holds back innovation, and 56% of all firms saw no effect.

sources.title: Randstad-ifo-Studie: Fehlerkultur in Unternehmen (presseportal)

failure.text: In a YouGov survey commissioned by AXA (May 2024, 2,132 people), 25% said they cannot admit mistakes at work, rising to 44% among those under 25. 23% expect negative consequences if they disclose a mistake.

sources.title: AXA Studie zur Fehlerkultur im Job

failure.text: An article on an EY survey (around 2023, about 1,000 people in machinery, automotive, finance and other sectors) reports that 64% of managers did not admit, or only partly admitted, their own mistakes from the past two years.

sources.title: EY-Studie zur Fehlerkultur (dashoefer)

failure.text: In a survey by the industry association Bitkom (October 2024), 70% of companies said data protection hinders digitalization. At 63% of companies, innovation projects failed or never started because of data protection rules. A follow-up survey put that share at 77%.

failure.text: A study comparing GDPR coverage in Germany, France, the UK, and the US (Sanford & Yasseri, 2021) found that German and French media tend to frame privacy as a fundamental right, while British and American media focus on compliance and commerce.

sources.title: Sanford & Yasseri — The Kaleidoscope of Privacy (arXiv 2104.04074)

feedback.text: The Culture Map (2014) places Germany on the direct side of Evaluating. Meyer says Germans tend to deliver negative feedback without softening it.

sources.title: Erin Meyer — Eight-scale Tool for Mapping Cultural Differences (chart: The Culture Map, 2014)

feedback.text: One book review says Germany is on the confrontational side of Disagreeing, but that German disagreement is objective and emotionally restrained, unlike the expressive confrontation found in France.

sources.title: Deploy Yourself — The Culture Map book review

feedback.text: A 2021 review of factors behind pull request decisions cites a study (Rastogi et al., ESEM 2018) finding that pull requests are more likely to be accepted when the submitter and reviewer are in the same country.

sources.title: Pull Request Decision Explained: An Empirical Overview (arXiv 2105.13970)

hierarchy.text: Meyer classifies Germany as more hierarchical than the United States but also more inclined to build consensus before deciding.

sources.title: Erin Meyer — Eight-scale Tool for Mapping Cultural Differences (chart: The Culture Map, 2014)

hierarchy.text: Under BetrVG §87(1) no. 6, the works council (Betriebsrat) has codetermination rights over technical equipment that can monitor employees' behavior or performance. What counts is whether it can be used for monitoring. In 2022 the Federal Labor Court (1 ABR 20/21) applied this to Microsoft Office 365.

sources.title: hensche.de — BAG, Beschluss vom 08.03.2022, 1 ABR 20/21
lulius.ai — § 87 BetrVG: Mitbestimmung bei Software und KI

hierarchy.text: At N26 in Berlin, management opposed a works council election in 2020 and fought it as far as a court injunction. A works council was still elected in November and December that year, with turnout of about 30%.

sources.title: CNBC — German digital bank N26 faces outcry from staff over management
Wikipedia — N26

communication.text: The Culture Map places Germany on the low-context side of Communicating. Meyer says Germans state things explicitly, repeat points to confirm them and prefer to put things in writing.

sources.title: Erin Meyer — Eight-scale Tool for Mapping Cultural Differences (chart: The Culture Map, 2014)

communication.text: SUP.10 in Automotive SPICE requires change requests to be linked to the affected work products and analyzed in advance. In regulated industries, documentation is a contractual requirement as well.

sources.title: VDA QMC — Automotive SPICE PAM v4.0

communication.text: Citing the Deutscher Startup Monitor 2024, startuprad.io reports that English is the main working language at over 55.8% of Berlin startups. For the share of employees from abroad, the same article gives two figures, 30.8% and 42.3%.

sources.title: startuprad.io — The rise of Berlin startups

work.text: Eurostat puts average actual weekly hours in Germany in 2024 (ages 20 to 64, full-time and part-time combined) at 33.9, below the EU average of 36.0.

sources.title: Eurostat — People in the EU worked on average 36 hours per week

work.text: In its decision of 13 September 2022 (1 ABR 22/21), the Federal Labor Court held that employers must record working time. Trust-based working time (Vertrauensarbeitszeit), where employees manage their own hours, remains lawful.

sources.title: Federal Labour Court (BAG): 1 ABR 22/21, decision of 13 September 2022

work.text: According to Destatis, SMEs as defined by the EU made up 99.3% of all enterprises and 54% of persons employed in 2024. IfM Bonn defines the Mittelstand by the unity of ownership and management rather than by size, so it is a separate concept.

sources.title: Destatis — Small and medium-sized enterprises

work.text: According to a site compiling Eurostat data, about 13.2% of employed people usually worked from home in 2025, above the EU average. Destatis figures cited by Euronews put the share at about 24% in 2024 when occasional home working is included.

Euronews — Working from home in Europe

work.text: Germany's Dismissal Protection Act (KSchG) does not apply its standard dismissal rules to establishments with 10 or fewer employees (5 or fewer for staff hired before 2004). The works council must be heard before any dismissal, and a dismissal without that hearing is void.

variance: In regulated industries such as automotive, upfront design and documentation under ASPICE and ISO 26262 are contractual requirements. Berlin's VC-backed startups, by contrast, often run international teams that work in English and should be read as a different culture.
Openness about mistakes depends heavily on company size. In the Randstad-ifo survey (2026), 28% of large firms said mistakes are discussed openly, against 62% of small firms.
Codetermination through a works council is taken for granted at traditional companies but contested at startups, as the 2020 N26 case shows.
Germany's Hofstede UAI score is 65, below France's 86 and lower than the common image of Germans as extremely risk-averse would suggest.
No study was found that links national culture directly to code review or postmortem practice, so statements in this area depend heavily on inference.
